QuestionStmt.S: The value of $$\int_{1}^{4} \log[x] \, dx$$, where $[x]$ is the greatest integer function less than or equal to $x$ is equal to

Solution.S: Let $I = \int_{1}^{4} \log[x] \, dx$. Splitting the integral at integer points: $$I = \int_{1}^{2} \log1 \, dx + \int_{2}^{3} \log2 \, dx + \int_{3}^{4} \log3 \, dx$$ $$= 0 + \log2 \cdot (3-2) + \log3 \cdot (4-3) = \log2 + \log3 = \log(2 \times 3) = \log6.$$ Hence the correct option is B.
